title: How programs send email: SMTP vs HTTP email APIs
subject: cs

questions.question: The standard protocol used to send email to a mail server is called _____.
questions.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol is the set of rules every mail server understands for receiving messages.

questions.question: Which port is mainly used for email passed between mail servers?
questions.explanation: Port 25 is the server-to-server door. B is tempting, but 587 is for programs that log in to submit mail.

questions.question: Is it true that port 587 encrypts the connection from the very first byte?
questions.explanation: On 587 the conversation starts in plain text and STARTTLS switches on encryption. Encryption from the first byte is port 465 (implicit TLS).

questions.question: What is the difference between STARTTLS and implicit TLS?
questions.answer: STARTTLS starts unencrypted, then upgrades the same connection to encryption. Implicit TLS is encrypted from the start.
questions.explanation: STARTTLS starts unencrypted, then upgrades the same connection to encryption. Implicit TLS is encrypted from the start. Both encrypt before the password is sent.

questions.question: Is it true that an app password is just your normal account password typed into a program?
questions.explanation: It is a separate password created for one program. Your real password stays private.

questions.question: Why is an app password safer than putting your real password in a program?
questions.answer: If it leaks, you delete just that app password; your real password and 2-step verification stay safe.
questions.explanation: If it leaks, you delete just that app password. Your real password and your 2-step verification stay safe, and the rest of your account is protected.

questions.question: Besides the older IPv4 address, a server name can also resolve to a newer _____ address.
questions.explanation: DNS can return both kinds. A program may try IPv6 first, even if the machine cannot reach IPv6.

questions.question: A server has no IPv6 route, and a program tries the IPv6 address first. What happens?
options: The connection fails with "Network is unreachable"
The email is sent, only more slowly
The mail server rejects the password
questions.explanation: There is no path to any IPv6 address, so the connection cannot even start. Forcing IPv4 avoids this. D is wrong because the program never reaches the login step.

questions.question: Why do many cloud hosts block outgoing SMTP ports on their free plans?
options: SMTP is too slow for their servers
SMTP only works on home computers
To stop people using free servers to send spam
To force programs to use IPv6
questions.explanation: Free servers are easy for spammers to abuse, which harms the host's reputation. A is tempting, but speed has nothing to do with it.

questions.question: What does a program send to prove who it is when it calls an HTTP email API?
options: An API key in a request header
questions.explanation: The API key is a secret token, usually sent in the Authorization header. D is tempting, but app passwords are for SMTP logins.

questions.question: Is it true that an HTTP email API can still deliver to normal inboxes like Gmail?
questions.explanation: The service receives your request, then sends the email with SMTP from its own servers, so it lands in any inbox.

questions.question: Why does an HTTP email API work on a host that blocks SMTP?
questions.answer: It uses HTTPS on port 443, like all web traffic, which hosts do not block; the SMTP part happens on the email service's servers.
questions.explanation: It uses HTTPS on port 443, the same door as all web traffic, which hosts do not block. The SMTP part happens on the email service's servers, not yours.

questions.question: Is it true that the Reply-To header decides who receives the email?
questions.explanation: The To header decides who receives it. Reply-To only decides where the answer goes when the reader presses "Reply".
